newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Super-Sol rated a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Super-Sol rated a buy.

text.p: Carnegie Emerging Markets initiated coverage of Israel's Super-Sol Ltd with a buy recommendation saying the shares were a good value in comparison with other emerging market food retailers.

"Super-Sol has attracted a well merited premium rating from the investment community reflecting strong sales performance, a highly attractive sector in general and a top management team," analyst Stephen Levey wrote in a report.
"We believe that on a 1997 PER (price/earnings ratio) of only 14.4x and 11.8x 1998 EPS (earnings per share) the company deserves a larger premium to the market to fully reflect these qualities."
The market PER was estimated at 13.9.
London-based Carnegie estimated EPS would rise to 6.56 shekels in 1997 and 8.02 in 1998 from 5.90 shekels in 1996.

Levey noted there has been concern that Super-Sol overpaid in acquiring the supermarket business of retailer Shekem Ltd . Super-Sol paid 250 million shekels plus the value of the merchandise in stock.
"We believe that on a two-year time horizon this acquisition will be seen as an extremely shrewd business decision," he said.

Carnegie expects Super-Sol to make a decision regarding the sale or closure of its Super-Office outlets this year. "With losses of over 12 million shekels in 1996, the removal of this business would provide significant upside earnings potential not built into our forecasts," the report said.

Levey said Super-Sol trades at a lower relative PER than other leading food retailers in Turkey, Portugal and Greece. "We believe it deserves a higher relative rating to take account of the fact that foreign competition in Israel is almost impossible due to the issue of kosher food," the report said.
